claim: The 'DVD collection is disc-rot / a lost cause' conclusion was wrong: Verify-Rip.ps1 counted every ffmpeg stderr line as an error, but ffmpeg's null muxer floods stderr with benign 'non monotonically increasing dts' warnings on DVD VOB rips, so clean rips (Raiders, Conan) were falsely quarantined; the fix filters timestamp-class muxer noise.
trigger: when Verify-Rip marks a DVD rip CORRUPT with thousands of identical dts-warning stderr lines
before declaring a DVD collection degraded based on verify verdicts

claim: Windows PowerShell 5.1 `2>` redirection wraps a native exe's stderr lines at host width, so Verify-Rip counted the split fragments of benign ffmpeg dts warnings as decode errors and false-quarantined clean DVD rips; capture raw stderr with Start-Process -RedirectStandardError and count corruption via a positive genuine-error regex instead.
trigger: when a Verify-Rip verdict shows decode-error count equal to benign-warning count
before using PowerShell 2> to capture a native exe's stderr for line counting

claim: MSYS/Git-Bash `tail -F` on Windows opens a file without FILE_SHARE_WRITE, so tailing the active pipeline log at D:\claude\plex\pipeline\logs silently blocked the daemons' Add-Content writes ('file being used by another process'); use poll-based monitors (wc -l + sed of new ranges) instead of tail -F.
trigger: when the pipeline log stops updating while rips clearly continue
before starting a tail -F monitor on a file a Windows daemon writes

claim: The recurring frozen-pipeline-log mystery was orphaned tail.exe/grep.exe processes left behind when Monitor live-tail tasks were stopped (TaskStop does not kill Git Bash children); they hold the log without FILE_SHARE_WRITE so Write-Log's Add-Content drops lines silently — kill the orphans to resume logging and never tail -F daemon-written files.
trigger: when a log file's LastWriteTime stops advancing while the daemon is demonstrably still working
after stopping any Monitor that ran tail -F, when checking for leftover tail.exe/grep.exe processes

claim: Match-Runtime.ps1 (disc-lookup layer 2) was built and live-validated 2026-06-30: when TheDiscDb does not auto-accept, it confirms title guesses against TMDB's known runtime (240s tolerance) via Find-MovieByRuntime and returns the runtime-matched MainIndex; with no TMDB key it no-ops to the heuristic, and daemons must only be restarted when no makemkvcon/ffmpeg is running.
trigger: when TheDiscDb does not auto-accept a disc identity
before restarting Reel-AutoRip daemons while makemkvcon or ffmpeg is in flight

claim: Find-MovieByRuntime must match the TMDB runtime ONLY against the disc's MAIN feature (longest title, >=2400s) — matching any title let a 6-minute extra match a short film and rip 'LAST_STARFIGHTER' as the wrong movie; guesses are now ordered cleaned-label first and the non-accepted DiscDb candidate last, and identity layers must be adversarially tested with decoy titles before daemons go live.
trigger: when a runtime-match identity selects a title far shorter than a feature film
before enabling a new disc-identity layer on live rip daemons

trigger: before placing TV episodes numbered from makemkv title order
when multiple discs of a season finish processing out of disc order

claim: On Babylon 5 R1 DVDs each disc holds a contiguous 4-episode block but makemkv title order WITHIN the disc is scrambled, so disc-order numbering plus the TvEpsPerDisc-derived EpStart still mislabels every episode — per-title content identification (subtitle proper-noun signatures, e.g. Identify-B5S2.ps1) is required to order within the block.
trigger: before numbering TV episodes from makemkv scan order within a disc
when placing Babylon 5 DVD rips into season folders

claim: The Plex SQLite library DB on C: survives loss of the media drive and lists every ripped title with its original file path (join metadata_items->media_items->media_parts, path in media_parts.file), so diffing DB rows against surviving files yields the exact re-rip manifest; query a COPY of the WAL-mode db with Plex SQLite.exe, and the API still answers with .LocalAdminToken as X-Plex-Token even when Preferences.xml is missing.
trigger: when a Plex media volume is lost and the re-rip list is needed
before opening the live Plex SQLite DB while the service is running

claim: On Windows, makemkvcon reads its registration key from the registry at HKCU\Software\MakeMKV value app_Key, not from %APPDATA%\MakeMKV\settings.conf (a Linux/Mac mechanism); a missing key makes retail Blu-rays fail with MSG:5053 + MSG:5010 and TCOUNT:0 while DVDs still work, and the ~monthly beta key must be refreshed into the registry.
trigger: when makemkvcon emits MSG:5053 shareware and TCOUNT:0 on a retail Blu-ray
before refreshing the MakeMKV beta key on Windows

claim: When appending a downmixed compat audio track (Add-CompatAudio.ps1), ffmpeg's channel count must use the audio-relative specifier -ac:a:N — the global -ac:N is silently ignored and the AAC track keeps the 8-channel source layout; also build per-stream flags as interpolated strings, since concatenation produced a parse where ffmpeg treated '256k' as an output filename.
trigger: when an appended AAC compat track comes out with the source channel count instead of stereo
before composing ffmpeg per-stream option strings in PowerShell

claim: Plex's .LocalAdminToken rotates (after claiming the server or a restart), so cached token copies go stale and admin API calls return HTTP 401 while /identity still returns 200; point PlexTokenFile directly at the live .LocalAdminToken and re-read it when debugging Plex 401s.
trigger: when Plex library-refresh API calls return 401 but /identity returns 200
before caching the Plex admin token to a separate file

claim: PowerShell treats [ ] in paths as glob wildcards, so bracketed staging-folder timestamps made every -Path file op silently fail — rips logged 'Produced 0 files' though makemkv wrote them, and Move-Item+cleanup deleted un-moved Babylon 5 episodes; any path that may contain disc-label characters must use -LiteralPath, and Place-One must Test-Path-confirm moves before logging Placed.

before writing PowerShell file operations on staging paths derived from disc labels

claim: PowerShell Start-Job children die when their foreground tool call returns — a recovery job's exit ran Process-Staged's cleanup and deleted staging before anything was placed — so staging is now deleted only if ($completed -and -not $failed), and detached long-running work must use the harness run_in_background or the long-lived daemon's own Start-Job, never Start-Job in a one-shot foreground call.
trigger: before launching long-running recovery work via Start-Job inside a foreground tool call
when a staging folder disappears after a worker was killed early

claim: The 2h RipTimeoutSec killed a ~32GB Blu-ray mid-write on the slow LG GGC-H20L (~6-8 MB/s) under dual-drive contention, leaving a truncated file without the Matroska magic that Verify-Rip still scored only 'MINOR' and placed; RipTimeoutSec was raised to 14400s, big BDs should rip solo, and Verify-Rip needs an ffprobe container/header check, not just decode-error counting.
trigger: when a large Blu-ray rip is killed exactly at RipTimeoutSec
before trusting decode-error counts alone to validate a ripped file

claim: TheDiscDb needs no API — it is an open Git repo (github.com/TheDiscDb/data) of per-disc JSON where discNN.json carries ContentHash plus per-title SourceFile/SegmentMap/Duration and Season/Episode, matchable locally against our own makemkvcon -r info scan by structural fingerprint; coverage is heavily Blu-ray, so a DVD pressing of a catalogued title (e.g. B5 on DVD) will NOT match and must fall through to runtime-match or operator override.
trigger: before integrating disc-identity lookup against TheDiscDb
when a DVD pressing fails to match TheDiscDb despite the title being catalogued

claim: Never delete a source folder after a batch copy without verifying destination count equals source count — an apostrophe in a FLAC filename made ffmpeg's copy silently fail, the loop continued, and rm -rf permanently deleted the un-copied track; for awkward filenames prefer metaflac in-place tag edits over ffmpeg re-mux.
trigger: before removing a source folder after any batch copy
when batch-processing files whose names contain apostrophes, quotes, or brackets

trigger: when a rip's output write rate stays below the crawl floor after the grace period
before writing synthetic slow-writer tests against the crawl-abort logic
